target_customer: Procurement and compliance teams at mid-sized and large companies in Latin America, mainly Brazil, that must onboard and vet many suppliers
problem: Supplier registration, qualification (homologacao) and approval is slow, manual and document heavy, which raises lead time and cost for enterprise buyers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for enterprise procurement teams, integrated with ERP and procurement suites
product_category: Supplier relationship management and supplier onboarding

founders.name: Leo Cavalcanti
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CEO on the YC page. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Cirdes Henrique
founders.background_notes: Listed as CTO and organizer of Tropical on Rails on the YC page. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: A workflow SaaS for supplier registration with validation against Brazilian fiscal and banking data and ERP integrations. The hard parts were integrations and data validation, not research-grade technology.

defensibility.rationale: Deep ERP and procurement suite integrations and enterprise supplier data networks (the company now reports 650,000 connected suppliers) create switching costs, though the early product was a workflow tool others could copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company's own site lists SAP Ariba and Coupa as integration partners rather than rivals, so the global suites appear to be complements for this wedge. No acquisition or copying found.

market_need_then: Large Brazilian buyers need to qualify many suppliers against fiscal, legal and risk criteria. The company later cites a customer cutting homologation from 42 to 8 days, which is a vendor claim. No dated 2019 to 2020 demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses linkana.com, exact name .com. No acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product-led enterprise tone with an 'autopilot' framing on the website

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. It is a B2B name known within Brazilian procurement, with enterprise logos on its site but no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Linkana remains active and, per its own site, sells to large Brazilian enterprises such as Suzano, Raizen and Gerdau, with over 200 procurement leaders and 1,500 users claimed. Public funding is thin: aggregators show roughly 200 thousand dollars from YC, Latitud, Endeavor and Plug and Play, so growth appears capital light. The company has stayed a niche enterprise SaaS in a single region and no exit has occurred.
notes: Funding figures are aggregator only and conflict (CB Insights about 200K over several rounds with a Seed round dated 2022-05 and an accelerator round in 2023-08; Caplight 162K; FundedIQ one round in 2020-03), so no rounds are recorded. Investors named by aggregators: YC, Latitud, Endeavor Scale-Up Brazil, Plug and Play, Google for Startups Accelerator Brazil. Founding year is 2018 on the YC page and 2019 on one aggregator. Competitors: CB Insights lists Gedanken, Kodiak Hub and Gainfront but without dates, so none are recorded; the list is empty because nothing dated near the 2020 batch was found. The about page returned 404.
